title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a computation in 2x2 matrices. It belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', a sequel to La Longue Marche, which studies Galois-type actions on SL2(Z)-type groups through equations on generators.

Setting:
- σ∞ = [[0,1],[-1,0]] is the order-4 elliptic element.
- ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] is the order-6 elliptic element, with ρ^{-1} = [[1,-1],[1,0]].
- The unknown is a matrix u (underlined in the manuscript) to be found with prescribed determinant μ (eq. 66) and prescribed commutator [u,ρ] = ±g (eqs. 65, 67, 68). The sign ε' records whether u is a similitude (u^t u = +det u) or an anti-similitude (u^t u = -det u).

The previous page explains how this ansatz was reached:
- A detour through parameters (a,b,c,d) led to Eisenstein-type norms c²+cd+d² = ε3/μ, with u0 = μ(cρ+d) in the centralizer of ρ.
- Grothendieck then arrived at the 'disconcertingly simple' formula (74): u = μ(tσ∞+u·1).
- This is μ times the image of the Gaussian integer u+ti in the centralizer of σ∞. Its determinant is the norm t²+u² = ε2/μ.

The ε2 = +1 case (this page):
1. det u = μ²·(1/μ) = μ, which is (66).
2. The scalar μ cancels in the commutator, and (tσ∞+u)^{-1} = μ·[[u,-t],[t,u]].
3. He computes [u,ρ] = μ (u t;-t u) ρ (u -t; t u) ρ^{-1}. The intermediate products are (-t, u+t; -u, u-t)·(u-t, -u; u+t, -t).
4. The result is μ((u+t)²-ut+t², -t²; ut-t², u²+t²-ut) = (1+μt(u+t), -μt²; μt(u-t), 1-μut).
5. Using μ(u²+t²) = 1, this matches g from (65). The key identity is -1+μu(u+t) = μt(u-t).

I rechecked every matrix product and the identity; all are correct.

The ε2 = -1 case (end of page):
- Here one expects ε' = -1, i.e. u should be an anti-similitude.
- Grothendieck guesses 'au pif' that composing with the orthogonal reflection τ∞ = diag(-1,1) gives the answer: u = μτ∞(tσ∞+u).
- The next page verifies this and corrects the order of the factors to u = μ(tσ∞+u)τ∞.

Underlying structure: solutions are parametrized by norm-type equations in Z[i] (centralizer of σ∞) and Z[ω] (centralizer of ρ). The sign ε' is tied to whether -1 is a norm, conjecturally ε' = +1 iff p ≡ 1 (mod 4) by class field theory.
errors: In the final displayed product Grothendieck writes τ∞ as diag(-1,-1) instead of diag(-1,1). The resulting matrix is also miscomputed: diag(-1,1)·(u t;-t u) = (-u,-t;-t,u). On the next page he notices a sign inconsistency (getting the spurious condition ut=0) and fixes it by putting τ∞ on the right.

Minor: the (2,1) entry of the final ε2=+1 matrix is written μt(ut-t²) [as transcribed]; it should be μ(ut-t²) = μt(u-t). This is a slip of the pen only; the subsequent identity uses the correct μt(u-t).

ideas.what: Parametrizing solutions of a commutator/determinant equation in GL2 by elements of the centralizer of an elliptic element. Here u = μ(tσ∞+u) lies in the Gaussian torus Z[i] ⊂ M2 (for ρ, the Eisenstein torus Z[ω]); the determinant condition becomes a norm equation t²+u² = ε2/μ.
ideas.modern_name: Norm tori / CM tori attached to the elliptic points i and ω of SL2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Gauss, Eisenstein; standard in the theory of SL2(Z) and CM)

ideas.what: Producing anti-similitude solutions (u^t u = -det u) from similitude solutions by composing with an orthogonal reflection τ∞. The sign ε' is linked to the class of p mod 4.
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonal vs. anti-orthogonal similitudes; normalizer of a non-split torus; quadratic character χ_{-4}

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an explicit verification of a matrix-commutator identity plus a heuristic ansatz for the other sign case. It is correct, elementary, and serves a larger unpublished computation, but contains no new concept on its own.
transcription_corrections: The second matrix in the commutator is ρ = (0 1; -1 1), not (0 1; -1 0). The intermediate product (-t, u+t; -u, u-t) confirms this.
The final-entry slip '-t' in the last matrix is crossed/overwritten. The manuscript's last factor reads μ(-1 0; 0 -1) as written, which is itself an error for diag(-1,1).
The left marginal note reads roughly 'on pourrait aussi [?] utiliser les formules (78) §93' (unsure).
